business.title: Adaptive multi-scale YOLOv8s framework for defect detection in photovoltaic facilities
business.desc: Photovoltaic (PV) modules are widely used in building-integrated photovoltaic systems and renewable energy infrastructure. Accurate defect detection is essential for improving the reliability, energy efficiency, and sustainable operation of PV systems. However, existing deep learning-based inspection methods still suffer from missed detections, imprecise localisation of small defects, and limited robustness under complex operating conditions due to variations in defect scales and background interference. This study proposes an adaptive multi-scale attention-enhanced YOLOv8s framework (AMA-YOLOv8s) for intelligent PV module defect detection. Compared with the baseline YOLOv8s, the proposed framework incorporates three newly designed modules specifically developed for PV defect detection: the Adaptive Bottleneck Attention Mechanism (ABAM), Multi-scale Adaptive Fusion Module (MSAFM), and Adaptive Pooling Fusion Module (APFM). ABAM is introduced to enhance defect-related feature representation and suppress irrelevant background information, whereas MSAFM and APFM are designed to strengthen multi-scale feature fusion and improve the detection of small and irregular defects. In addition, a comprehensive PV defect dataset was constructed by integrating publicly available images, field-collected samples, and data augmentation strategies. Experimental results show that AMA-YOLOv8s achieves a precision of 93.2%, an F1-score of 92.7%, and an mAP@0.5 of 93.5% on the current evaluation dataset. Compared with the YOLOv8s baseline, the AMA-YOLOv8s provides incremental improvements in detection performance while maintaining a comparable real-time inference speed. Its overall performance is competitive with the evaluated detectors, although recent lightweight YOLO variants retain advantages in some individual metrics and computational complexity. These results demonstrate the practical effectiveness of the proposed coordinated attention and multi-scale feature-fusion design for PV defect detection.

business.title: Head-to-head comparison of [18F]FAPI and [18F]FDG PET/CT in the clinical value of hepatocellular carcinoma
business.desc: To investigate the clinical utility of fluorine-18-labeled fibroblast activation protein (FAP) inhibitor ([18F]FAPI) positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) relative to [18F]fluorodeoxyglucose ([18F]FDG) PET/CT for tumor detection and staging in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) patients. A cohort of 38 individuals (median age, 61 years; interquartile range, 56–68 years), all with pathologically confirmed primary or recurrent HCC, were enrolled. All participants underwent both [18F]FDG and [18F]FAPI PET/CT. Maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax), tumor-to-background ratio (TBR), metabolic tumor volume (MTV), FAP expression tumor volume (FTV), total lesion glycolysis (TLG), total lesion FAP expression (TLF), and clinical staging were compared. Each patient had at least one intrahepatic lesion confirmed by surgical resection or percutaneous biopsy. Histopathologic confirmation was available for 46/66 intrahepatic lesions, 3/56 lymph-node (LN) metastases, and 4/33 distant metastases; the remaining lesions were adjudicated using a composite reference standard based on multimodal imaging follow-up and treatment response. Additionally, correlations between PET imaging findings and serum biomarkers, comprising alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) and protein induced by vitamin K absence or antagonist II (PIVKA-II), were analyzed. The cohort included 32 primary and 6 recurrent HCC cases. [18F]FAPI PET/CT showed higher lesion detection rates than [18F]FDG PET/CT for primary intrahepatic lesions (96.7% vs. 60.0%; p < 0.001), LN metastases (94.6% vs. 80.4%; p = 0.021), and distant metastases (78.8% vs. 48.5%; p = 0.002). For primary intrahepatic lesions, [18F]FAPI PET/CT showed higher SUVmax (7.90 vs. 4.80, p < 0.001) and TBR (5.45 vs. 2.60, p < 0.001) than [18F]FDG PET/CT. In the patient-level volumetric analysis of the 32 initial-staging patients, FTV was 21.04 vs. MTV 13.75 (p < 0.001), and TLF was 135.36 vs. TLG 51.44 (p < 0.001). For LN metastases, [18F]FAPI PET/CT showed higher SUVmax (7.98 vs. 6.63, p = 0.048) and TBR (7.85 vs. 4.95, p < 0.001), as well as higher FTV than MTV (6.55 vs. 4.55, p < 0.001) and TLF than TLG (67.65 vs. 52.75, p < 0.001). Positive correlations were observed between [18F]FAPI PET/CT tumor uptake parameters and AFP and PIVKA-II levels (nominal p < 0.05). Relative to [18F]FDG, [18F]FAPI PET/CT produced staging changes in 19/32 patients undergoing initial staging, including 6 true upstagings, and identified 3 additional local recurrences; a FAPI-informed management change was implemented in 57.9% (22/38) of patients. Exploratory receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses yielded areas under the curve (AUCs) of 0.947, 0.921, 0.895, and 0.864 for SUVmax, TBR, FTV, and TLF, respectively. [18F]FAPI PET/CT showed higher lesion detection in selected HCC settings than [18F]FDG PET/CT for primary intrahepatic, lymph-node, and distant metastatic lesions and may provide complementary information for staging and treatment planning in this preliminary single-center cohort. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05810324; registered on 30 March 2023.

business.title: IGFBP5 knockdown is associated with improved early neurovascular regeneration after sciatic nerve injury
business.desc: Peripheral nerve injury (PNI) disrupts neurovascular integrity and leads to persistent sensory and motor dysfunction. Insulin-like growth factor binding protein 5 (IGFBP5) regulates insulin-like growth factor bioavailability and has also been implicated in apoptosis, fibrosis, and extracellular matrix remodeling; however, its role in peripheral nerve regeneration remains unclear. This study investigated the temporal expression pattern of IGFBP5 following sciatic nerve injury (SNI) and examined whether its suppression is associated with early neurovascular regenerative responses. A murine SNI model was established, and IGFBP5 was silenced using perineural delivery of lentiviral short hairpin RNA. Neurovascular remodeling, cellular responses, and stress-related changes were evaluated at 5 days post-injury, and functional recovery was assessed longitudinally up to 12 weeks. We observed that IGFBP5 expression was markedly increased in both proximal and distal nerve segments after injury. IGFBP5 knockdown was associated with increased endothelial and axonal marker signals, accompanied by enhanced Schwann cell– and macrophage-associated responses and reduced myelin-associated signals. In parallel, reduced oxidative and nitrosative stress and decreased apoptotic markers were detected, together with increased proliferative activity during the early phase of regeneration. In addition, IGFBP5 suppression was associated with increased phosphorylation of PI3K–AKT and ERK signaling pathways. Functional assessments indicated improved motor recovery and higher sciatic functional index scores compared with controls. Together, these findings suggest that IGFBP5 knockdown is associated with a more favorable early neurovascular microenvironment following peripheral nerve injury. Targeting IGFBP5 may represent a potential strategy to modulate early regenerative processes, although further studies are required to define its mechanistic role and long-term effects.

technology.title: Uncooled low-noise optomechanical sensors on thin-film lithium niobate
technology.desc: Optomechanical transduction harnesses the interaction between optical fields and mechanical motion to achieve sensitive measurement of weak mechanical quantities with inherently low noise. Lithium niobate combines low optical loss, strong piezoelectricity, a high intrinsic f × Qm factor, and low thermal conductivity, making it promising for exploring optomechanical platforms targeting thermal sensing applications. Here, we demonstrate an integrated optomechanical platform on thin-film lithium niobate with precisely engineered optical, mechanical, and thermal fields within a compact 40 μm-diameter footprint. The platform integrates suspended microring resonators with ultrathin central membranes, reducing effective mass and thermal capacitance while maintaining a high intrinsic optical quality factor Qo of 106 and a mechanical quality factor Qm of 1117, which increases to 5.1 × 104 upon optomechanical oscillation. The two-step etching suppresses thermal dissipation into the silicon substrate and enhances thermal sensitivity, achieving a temperature coefficient of frequency of −124 ppm K−1, a measurable loaded thermal response time of 7.2 μs, and a noise-equivalent power of 6.2 nW Hz−1/2 at 10 kHz and room temperature. This compact and scalable platform opens new opportunities for high-sensitivity thermal sensing and power detection and supports heterogeneous integration with infrared absorbers for uncooled infrared detection, thereby paving the way toward large-format infrared sensing arrays with low-noise, all-optical readout.
